assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskites went from a dye-sensitised-cell sensitiser to thin-film absorbers exceeding 25 percent efficiency within about fifteen years, a rare case of a new semiconductor family reshaping photovoltaics, LEDs and detectors. The chemistry of composition, crystallisation and defect control is central.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka first used perovskites as sensitisers (2009); Park's solid-state cell and Snaith's meso-superstructured and planar devices established the thin-film architecture; Gratzel, Kanatzidis and Seok also contributed decisively. Any three-person split omits major contributors; this is my best reading of the priority sequence.
assessment.maturity: Efficiency records are independently replicated worldwide and the field is mature scientifically. Long-term operational stability and lead toxicity remain open, but the discovery itself is not premature.
uncertainties: Credit split among six credited names is contested and I have not verified priority details independently
Stability and commercial durability not yet settled

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Surfactant-templated ordered mesoporous silicas (MCM-41, SBA-15) opened a new regime of pore size between zeolites and amorphous materials, and underpin catalysis, adsorption, drug delivery and hard-templating of carbons and metals. The structures were proven by electron microscopy and diffraction, which I know well from my own field.
assessment.attribution: The Mobil group (Kresge, Beck and colleagues) made MCM-41; Kuroda/Inagaki independently reported FSM-16; Stucky and Zhao extended the approach to larger pores and SBA-15; Ryoo extended it to carbons. A fair configuration is possible but the Mobil-versus-Japanese priority question and the later extensions need careful treatment.
assessment.maturity: Three decades of independent confirmation and broad industrial and academic use; the impact is established and recognition would not be premature, though the peak of activity has passed.
uncertainties: Priority between Mobil and Japanese FSM-16 work
Whether later extensions (SBA-15, carbon replicas) should share credit
Limited commercial catalytic penetration relative to the early promise

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Induced-proximity degradation converts the ubiquitin-proteasome system into a pharmacological tool, with PROTACs and molecular glues (including the mechanism of thalidomide analogues via cereblon) now in clinical trials and a clear conceptual novelty for drug discovery.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies launched the PROTAC concept (2001); Handa and Ito identified cereblon as the thalidomide target; Ciulli and Gray provided key chemical-probe advances. The prize configuration is crowded and not obviously fair to all.
assessment.maturity: Strong preclinical and mechanistic confirmation and many clinical candidates, but no approved PROTAC drug yet, so clinical validation is incomplete.
uncertainties: Absence of an approved PROTAC
Allocation between PROTAC concept and the molecular-glue/cereblon discovery
Eight credited names exceed three laureates

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Serial femtosecond crystallography at XFELs enables structure determination from micro- and nanocrystals at room temperature and time-resolved studies of reactions, a methodological relative of the small-crystal diffraction methods I work with.
assessment.attribution: Chapman led the diffraction-before-destruction concept and the first demonstrations; Fromme and Schlichting contributed key biological applications and time-resolved work; Hajdu proposed the original idea and its fate in the credited list is uncertain to me. A three-person prize is plausible.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed at several XFEL facilities, but access is limited and the impact on routine structural biology is so far narrower than cryo-EM or synchrotron methods.
uncertainties: Hajdu's role and status
Limited breadth of impact so far
Chemistry versus physics framing

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors make precise single-nucleotide changes without double-strand breaks, an engineered chemistry of deaminases on programmable DNA binders, with first clinical applications now emerging.
assessment.attribution: Liu led the work and Komor and Gaudelli were the first authors of the cytosine and adenine base editors; Nishida and Kondo reported a related cytidine deaminase fusion. Allocation beyond Liu is uncertain, and the 2020 prize already covered CRISPR.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly adopted and entering clinical trials, but clinical benefit is still being established; recognition may be early.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2020 CRISPR prize
Credit for Komor and Gaudelli versus Nishida and Kondo
Clinical outcomes are still early

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rational design of zeolites and molecular sieves with controlled pores and active sites, including organic structure-directing agents, new framework types and hierarchical systems, underlies much industrial catalysis and separation, and is a field I know closely through structure determination of zeolites.
assessment.attribution: Corma, Davis and Zones span catalytic design, framework discovery and structure-directing agents; Yu and Tsapatsis also contributed major advances. The discovery is diffuse and a clean single-discovery attribution is hard.
assessment.maturity: Decades of confirmation and major commercial use (cracking, SCR, MTO), so it is mature, but it is a broad field rather than one discrete discovery.
uncertainties: Diffuse discovery with many contributors
Possible overlap with B060 on porous materials
My field proximity may bias my view

assessment.nobel_worthiness: MXenes are a large new family of 2D transition-metal carbides and nitrides with tunable chemistry, used in energy storage, EMI shielding and catalysis; the original Ti3C2 report from Drexel in 2011 opened a field of hundreds of compositions.
assessment.attribution: Naguib, Gogotsi and Barsoum authored the founding work and have driven the field; the three names map cleanly to a three-person prize.
assessment.maturity: Intense growth and replication, though practical applications are still maturing and few real-world products exist; recognition may be somewhat premature.
uncertainties: Limited commercial deployment
Stability of MXenes in air and water
Relative importance compared with graphene

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Supported single-atom catalysts maximise atom efficiency and provide well-defined active sites that bridge homogeneous and heterogeneous catalysis; atomic-resolution electron microscopy was essential for identification.
assessment.attribution: The 2011 Fe1/FeOx work of Qiao, Zhang and colleagues, together with Liu's STEM work on isolated atoms, is the usual anchor; Datye, Wang and Li contributed to characterisation and theory. Earlier atomically dispersed catalysts complicate priority.
assessment.maturity: Widely reproduced, but debate about uniform site structure and stability under reaction conditions means the concept is still consolidating.
uncertainties: Earlier atomically dispersed catalysts complicate priority
Verification that active sites are truly single atoms
Industrial relevance still limited
